### The Role

We're looking for a Lead Product Marketing Manager to own how VectorShift's product shows up in the world. You'll sit at the intersection of product, sales, and the market — turning a fast-moving, technically deep platform into stories, materials, and moments that make people _get it_ and want it.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll set the product marketing strategy and execute against it directly,. The through-line of everything you do: taking something technical and making it land with audiences who don't live in the weeds of AI infrastructure.

### What You'll Do

**Product releases & launches.** Own the narrative and go-to-market for new features and products — write the release notes, launch blogs, changelogs, and announcement copy. Coordinate launches across product, sales, and social so every release lands with impact instead of slipping out quietly.

**Demo paths & product storytelling.** Design the demo flows and narratives that show VectorShift at its best — the "aha" sequences that turn a curious prospect into a believer. Partner with sales and solutions to make sure the story we tell matches the product they experience.

**Sales enablement & materials.** Build the collateral that helps sales win: one-pagers, pitch decks, battle cards, case studies, competitive positioning, and ROI narratives. Keep it current as the product and market evolve.

**Social & top-of-funnel content.** Drive our social presence and content engine — posts, threads, short-form explainers, and campaigns that build awareness and pull people into the funnel.

**Translate technical → non-technical.** This is the heartbeat of the role. Take complex capabilities (RAG, agentic workflows, integrations, the SDK) and make them clear, compelling, and obviously valuable to business buyers, operators, and non-technical decision-makers.

**Positioning & messaging.** Own our core positioning, value propositions, and messaging framework — and make sure it's consistent across the website, sales, product, and social.

**Market & competitive intelligence.** Stay close to customers, competitors, and the broader AI landscape, and feed those insights back into product and GTM strategy.

### What We're Looking For

* 2+ years in product marketing, with a track record of owning launches and GTM for technical products (developer tools, AI/ML, or B2B SaaS/infrastructure strongly preferred).
* Exceptional writer and storyteller — you can go from a dense technical spec to a crisp, persuasive narrative, and you have samples to prove it.
* Demonstrated ability to make technical concepts accessible to non-technical audiences.
* Comfortable operating with autonomy in a fast-moving startup — you'll define process where none exists and ship without a lot of scaffolding.
* Strong cross-functional partner who can work shoulder-to-shoulder with product, sales, and founders.
* Experience building sales enablement materials and running product launches end to end.
* Bonus: hands-on curiosity about AI tooling — you like actually _using_ the product, not just marketing it.

Zep manages, governs, and serves agent memory at enterprise scale. Enterprises build on Zep to run reliable, personalized agents across the business: millions of Context Graphs, served in under 200ms, inside their own VPCs and cloud deployments. Customers include Samsung, Zscaler, Twin Health, HoneyBook, and NASDAQ 100 and Fortune 500 technology companies. We also build Graphiti, our open-source context graph framework (30K+ GitHub stars).

What our customers' agents can reason about depends on the memory we retrieve and the memory we write. You own that loop. You build agents that improve retrieval. You finetune the models that extract memory, and the models that power those agents. You run the experiments and ship the result as production code.

We're hiring an engineer who builds agents and trains the models they run on.

We will measure you on whether retrieval and memory quality move, and on what reaches production.

You'll report to our founder, Daniel (2x founder, engineer, former head of ML at SparkPost), and join a team with pedigree at Scale AI, Dropbox, ActiveCampaign, DroneDeploy, and McKinsey.

## How we work

We're a small, distributed team that works closely together. We pair on hard problems, review each other's designs, and treat learning as part of the job rather than something that happens after hours. We ask a lot of questions: of customers, of teammates, of our own assumptions. When we find pain, we go fix it.

We expect the same back: ask questions early, push back when you disagree, and care about the people on the other end of the API.

## What you'll do

* Build agents that improve retrieval: query understanding, ranking, and what to pull into context.
* Finetune the models that extract, update, and consolidate memory on Zep's domain.
* Finetune the models that power those agents, so the retrieval loop and the agent get better together.
* Own the work from dataset creation through experiment design, evaluation, training, and a change that ships to production. Our engineers work the serving path alongside you.
* Build the eval harnesses that catch regressions in retrieval, memory quality, and agent task completion before a release ships.
* Write up what you find, including the results that killed an idea, so the rest of engineering can build on it.

## Your first 90 days

In your first week you pick up an open retrieval or memory-extraction problem and frame it as an experiment. By day 30 an agent or a finetune you built is in the product loop, or you have ruled the approach out and written up why. By day 90 you are three cycles in and the eval harness you built runs on every release.

## What we're looking for

* You have shipped production ranking, retrieval, or query understanding.
* You've built classical ML into a real product — logistic regression, SVMs, GBTs, single-layer perceptrons.
* You've shipped finetuned models to production. You know transformer architectures and training workflows, and you work in PyTorch.
* You have shipped a non-trivial agentic system to production. Not a prototype, not a thin wrapper over a chat-completion API.
* You have a research methodology: dataset creation and curation, experiment design, and evaluation. You can frame an open problem and design an experiment that answers it.
* You have built evaluation for retrieval, generation, or agent tasks: gold sets, offline metrics, online tests.
* You write strong Python, and you have enough production AWS to ship, monitor, and iterate on what you train.
* You have a Master's in Computer Science or equivalent experience.

## This role is probably NOT a fit if:

* Your shipped work is papers, prototypes, and demos.
* Your agent work is a wrapper over a chat-completion API, with no eval and no model you trained.
* You haven't finetuned a model that reached production.
* You need a research agenda handed to you before you move.

Competitive salary with a meaningful variable component tied to the number you own, plus significant founding-team equity - discussed openly in our first conversation. Full ownership of go-to-market at the ground floor of a new category, working directly with the founders.

The recruiter stays in control: every shortlist is approved by a human, and every relationship and offer is owned by the customer's team.

You'll be the first voice enterprise talent leaders hear from Alex, and a primary driver of enterprise revenue growth. You’ll own multi-stakeholder accounts with real hiring volume, procurement processes, and strong talent leaders.

Your day to day will include:

- **Enterprise pipeline generation:** Prospect into named enterprise accounts across phone, email, video, social, and events. Research the account, map the buying committee, and open conversations with senior stakeholders using messaging that speaks to their hiring volume, cost per hire, and enterprise procurement processes.

- **Multi-threaded outbound strategy:** Own the enterprise outbound motion end-to-end – account selection, segmentation, and personalized multi-channel sequences. Partner tightly with Account Executives on account plans, multi-threading across a committee, and hands-on support through pilots and evaluations.

- **Performance & pipeline ownership:** Consistently hit and beat pipeline-generation targets. Track your own metrics, show up prepared for pipeline and forecast reviews, and keep tuning targeting and messaging based on what the market tells you.

- **Data management & tooling:** Run a clean, well-documented process in Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Amplemarket, Nooks, and similar platforms – prospecting, follow-up, and reporting an enterprise AE can build on.

This role is based in office in San Francisco and reports to our SDR Manager.

## **Why join**

- **Ground floor of the enterprise motion:** We're building the enterprise playbook now. What you learn in the first 90 days shapes how Alex sells to enterprise buyers.

- **Exposure:** Work directly with Account Executives, Product, and cross-functional leadership to sharpen enterprise messaging and account strategy.

- **Impact:** Sell a product that changes how people get hired and gives every candidate a real interview instead of a resume screen.

- **Upside:** Competitive compensation, including commission and equity.

- **Benefits:** Healthcare, vision and dental insurance, 401(k), unlimited PTO, beautiful office in SF, company-paid lunches, and great company events.

### **About Corgi**

Corgi is building the infrastructure for the next generation of insurance. We are a technology company using AI, automation, and modern infrastructure to rethink how insurance is built, distributed, and operated.

We are a fast-moving company where teams are expected to take ownership, move quickly, and constantly improve how we do things.

We are looking for a **Performance Marketing Specialist** to own and improve Corgi's paid advertising engine.

This is **not a social media manager role or traditional brand marketing position**. We need someone who understands paid acquisition and enjoys looking at the numbers, identifying what is working, and continuously optimizing performance.

Ideally, you can also **design the ads yourself** rather than relying entirely on outside designers.

### **The Role**

You will be responsible for the day-to-day performance and creative development of Corgi's paid advertising campaigns.

You will work across the full advertising cycle:

**Create → Launch → Measure → Optimize → Test → Scale**

You will analyze campaign performance, identify opportunities, develop new creative, run experiments, and continuously improve cost per lead and overall acquisition performance.

* Manage and optimize paid advertising campaigns across platforms such as Meta, Google, YouTube, and other relevant channels.
* Monitor campaign performance, budgets, conversion rates, cost per lead, and other key acquisition metrics.
* Continuously optimize campaigns based on performance data.
* Develop and test new ad concepts, messaging, formats, audiences, and landing-page approaches.
* Design advertisements and other marketing creative yourself.
* Create variations of existing creative to systematically test different hooks, headlines, visuals, layouts, and calls to action.
* Identify underperforming campaigns and diagnose why they are underperforming.
* Scale campaigns and creative that are producing strong results.
* Build structured A/B testing programs.
* Track performance and maintain clear reporting on what is working and what is not.
* Work with the broader Corgi team to improve the path from advertisement → lead → customer.
* Analyze lead quality, not simply lead volume.
* Help develop a repeatable creative testing and optimization process.
* Research competitors and advertising trends for ideas worth testing.
* Stay current on changes to advertising platforms, targeting capabilities, attribution, and creative best practices.
* Coordinate with outside vendors when additional production or specialized expertise is needed.

### **What We're Looking For**

We're less concerned with whether your previous title was "Performance Marketing Manager" and more concerned with whether **you know how to make advertising work**.

You should have:

* Experience running or optimizing paid digital advertising campaigns.
* Strong analytical instincts and comfort working with performance data.
* A/B testing experience and an understanding of conversion optimization.
* Experience with Meta Ads and/or Google Ads.
* Strong attention to detail.
* The ability to look at campaign data and turn it into concrete action.
* An understanding of how creativity affects advertising performance.
* Strong visual and design instincts.
* The ability to create, modify, and iterate on advertising creative yourself.
* A highly iterative mindset—you should naturally want to test version B when version A works.
* Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple campaigns and experiments simultaneously.

Ideally, You Can Also:

* Work comfortably in Figma, Adobe Creative Suite, Canva, or similar design tools.
* Edit short-form video for advertisements.
* Build landing pages or work with someone who does.
* Understand basic attribution and conversion tracking.
* Work with pixels, events, UTMs, and analytics platforms.
* Understand direct-response advertising and lead generation.
* Have experience with financial services, insurance, technology, or other performance-driven businesses.
* Have experience taking a campaign from initial concept through significant scale.

### **What This Role Is Not**

This is **not**:

* Influencer marketing.
* Community management.
* PR.
* Brand partnerships.
* A role primarily focused on organic social media.
* A role where an agency does all of the advertising work for you.

We are specifically looking for someone who wants to **own paid acquisition performance and creative optimization**.

We are hiring two ML Engineers / Researchers to help build the next generation of Knowtex's AI stack.

We are looking for researchers with deep expertise in one of two areas:

- Speech & Audio: Build state-of-the-art medical speech-to-text systems using our large proprietary dataset of real-world clinical audio, with the goal of bringing more of our speech stack in-house.

- Large Language Models: Develop and optimize models for clinical documentation and structured clinical reasoning, improving quality, cost, latency, and control.

You do not need to be an expert in both areas. We are looking for exceptional depth in either speech/audio modeling or LLMs.

These are research-heavy roles with a direct path to production. You will design experiments, build datasets and evaluation systems, train and fine-tune models, and work closely with engineering and clinical teams to deploy successful approaches at scale.

- Research approaches for improving medical terminology recognition, speaker attribution, punctuation, timestamps, and robustness across accents and clinical environments

- Build rigorous speech evaluation frameworks beyond traditional WER, including medical terminology and clinically significant error measurement

- Explore modern speech architectures, self-supervised learning, speech foundation models, and audio-language models

- Evaluate open-weight and proprietary model architectures and determine where fine-tuning, distillation, structured generation, or task-specific models can outperform general-purpose API-based approaches

- Fine-tune and post-train models using Knowtex's proprietary clinical datasets

- Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for clinical accuracy, hallucinations, completeness, formatting, and clinician preferences

- Research approaches for reducing inference cost and latency while maintaining or improving clinical quality

### Across Both Tracks

- Move quickly from idea → dataset → experiment → evaluation → production

- Design experiments that clearly measure whether an approach improves real-world clinical outcomes

- Build datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation infrastructure that make model improvements measurable and reproducible

- Collaborate closely with clinicians, applied ML engineers, and platform engineers

- Take successful research beyond prototypes and help deploy models into production

- Balance model quality with latency, inference cost, reliability, and scalability

**Distribution is the hardest problem every company has.** Getting a product in front of people, over and over, in a way that works. 

Today that means an army of humans making creative, testing it, reading the numbers, and doing it again next week. It doesn't scale, and it's the single biggest tax on every consumer brand in the world.

We think that changes. The billion-dollar companies of the next decade will look different. They won't scale linearly with headcount — they'll be run by fleets of AI agents running growth.

**Gooseworks is building self-improving AI agents that run growth for consumer brands — ads, UGC, organic — end to end.**

It’s early - this is just a few months old, but we have very strong pull and are growing fast:

* **200+ paying users**
* **30,000+ ad creatives generated by our users in the last 2 months**

We're a YC company based in San Francisco, and **we run the company on agent harnesses ourselves**.

### The role

You will **own** **growth and distribution** for GooseWorks. 

Your job will be to **build the systems to scale content**, and having the **creative taste and judgement** to improve them.

More specifically, you will own:

* **Creator channels, AI-operated.** You design the niche, the format, the hooks, the content, everything and use our AI creative agent to make organic social content at SCALE.
* **Our voice on X and LinkedIn**. Not "brand content", value content and stories that get noticed.
* **The taste layer of our creative agent.** You'll teach our creative agent what "good" means. It's the highest-leverage work at this company.
* **Launches.** Narrative, assets, video, sequencing, day-of. End to end, from a blank page.

---

### What we're looking for

1. **Taste.** You know what good content looks like. You have a great sense of design. You understand what people resonate with.
2. **Proof-of-work:** We need to see that you can make short-form that performs. IG, TikTok, YouTube, etc.
3. **Technical AI video skills.** You know what it takes to make great content using AI, and you’ve already been doing it.
4. **You think in systems.** We’re not looking for someone to write content. We’re looking for someone to build the thing that does.
5. **You live inside AI agents.** Claude Code, Codex, etc. You understand what a harness is and how to build one.

**Strong preferences for:**

* **a technical background**
* **proven content creator muscle**

---

### This is a 0→1 job

That means:

* **High ownership**: You'll own channels end-to-end, whatever that might mean. You’ll have autonomy and a high degree of creative control.
* **Lots of experimentation**: You’ll try lots of things fast and double down on what works.
* **Messy problems, fast loops.** Ship daily, execute is measured in hours, not weeks.
* **You're part of the founding team.**

# Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain?

The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain for getting secondhand fashion from donation to resale is completely offline, manual and broken.

Fleek is fixing this. **Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice.** We're building the infrastructure powering the global secondhand clothing trade, through a B2B marketplace and the AI systems digitising the supply chain behind it.

Through Fleek, vintage stores, online resellers and retail buyers source graded secondhand inventory directly from wholesalers and rag houses across multiple countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise items with just a photo. Turning what has historically been an opaque and manual trade into a structured, searchable and tradable global inventory layer.

Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill while tripling in size year-on-year. We're backed by some of the world's best investors, including a16z, Y Combinator and HV Capital, alongside world-class angels who helped build Depop, Shopify, and Postmates.

Today, we serve thousands of resellers and retailers across the UK, Europe and the US. With the secondhand fashion market projected to reach $350B by 2027, Fleek is building the AI-native operational and financial backbone for secondhand commerce globally.

We're looking for people who want to build something that matters and move fast doing it. Sounds good? Keep reading.

# About the Role

We're hiring a Special Projects Lead to take Fleek's new category bets from thesis to proven economics. Each is a new business line that could add £5M+ in GMV, opening a new supply category or a new sourcing geography for the marketplace. Here's what makes these bets unusually winnable. Fleek already owns the demand. Most of the live bets sell to buyers who transact on Fleek today, so they're a supply-first test rather than a two-sided cold start. Your job on a new bet is to find and onboard the supply, sell it into demand that already exists and read the economics fast.

Every bet runs through the same gates. If a bet misses its gates, you kill it with evidence and move to the next one. If it works and you're running it well, you don't have to hand it off. You scale into owning the category, with supply, acquisition and ops building out under you. Think of this seat as a venture builder inside Fleek.

One thing this is not. We're not building a sales team or a sales culture, and this is not an AE or account manager role with a new title. You'll work directly with the founders and our commercial lead, close to the centre of the company.

# What You'll Do

* **Run bets through the gates:** take each bet from market research to first suppliers to first GMV to a feasible-or-not call, with win metrics and kill metrics defined before you start.
* **Go where the supply is:** get on planes. You'll visit suppliers, graders and rag houses in the markets your bets open up, because this trade is built face to face and the best stock never gets listed anywhere.
* **Sell supply into live demand:** onboard brands, brokers, graders and wholesalers, then get Fleek's existing buyers transacting on the new inventory. The sell is fast, informal and relationship-led, over WhatsApp and Instagram as often as in a boardroom.
* **Make the kill calls:** hold a clear view of unit economics and the competitive landscape on every bet. Double down or cut on evidence, not attachment.
* **Be the ops function, for now:** work out importer-of-record structures, duties, freight cost and last mile for each new flow.
* **Ride the AI infrastructure:** our acquisition team has spent months building the agentic outreach and enrichment engine. You'll plug your bets into it and extend it, rather than building from a blank page or adding headcount.
* **Learn the actual trade:** how stock is graded, routed and priced across markets, and who's sitting on good inventory that nobody has approached. You'll get deep in it fast.

# What You Bring

* **Zero-to-one is your natural habitat.** You've built something from nothing as a founder, an early employee or the person who started a new line inside an existing company. You've operated without a playbook and you didn't wait for one.
* **Operator and commercial in one person.** You build the machine and you carry the number. You're not pure strategy and you're not pure sales, and you're comfortable being measured on GMV within your first quarter.
* **AI fluency.** You work with agents and automations daily and you'd rather build a workflow than repeat a task.

**Strong signals on top of that:**

* An instinct for physical goods. You understand inventory, margins and trading relationships, or you've worked around fashion, resale or marketplaces.
* Deals you structured yourself, at any size, that didn't exist before you wrote them.
* Exposure to cross-border trade, logistics or supply chain operations.

**Nice to Have**

* Direct experience in resale, surplus or secondary-market inventory
* Experience launching a new market, geography or product line from scratch
* Established networks in international sourcing markets

# What You'll Get

* Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it
* Comprehensive healthcare coverage
* A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London
* Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!)
* Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek
* Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office
* A disproportionate level of responsibility and the opportunity to drive massive impact

**How We Work**

Fleek is an in-office company. We're based at Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East). We operate a fully in-person culture at our office in Shoreditch, with trust-based flexibility. We hire adults and trust them to perform.

**The Practicalities**

* **Location:** London HQ, Commercial Street, E1 (Liverpool Street / Aldgate East)
* **Stage:** Post-Series B, hyper-growth
* **Team:** 200 across three geographies
* **Culture:** High ownership, non-hierarchical, fast-moving. Founder-led with strong opinions loosely held.

# Our Values

Five values shape how we work at Fleek:

* **Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself:** Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach.
* **Absolute Ownership:** The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done.
* **Curiosity Leads the Way:** Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate.
* **Talk to the Customer:** Deeply understand their challenges, motivations, and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre.
* **Embrace Diversity:** A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter.

**About Saturn**

Saturn is a Series A-backed fintech transforming how financial advice is delivered.

We operate in one of the world’s largest industries. Wealth and asset managers oversee more than $100 trillion and generate over $1 trillion in annual revenue, yet much of the infrastructure used to manage that wealth remains fragmented, manual and institution-specific.

Saturn is starting with the productivity and compliance systems used by financial advisers.

**Our story**

Saturn joined Y Combinator in 2024 and became one of the fastest-growing B2B companies in its batch.

We grew organically to a meaningful share of the UK financial advice market before acquiring the legacy leader, one of the industry’s most established compliance rule engine and suitability businesses, in 2025.

That acquisition combined AI-native product engineering with more than two decades of regulatory expertise, proprietary compliance logic and deep industry distribution.

Within two years of launch, Saturn became the leading provider of AI transformation to UK financial advice firms, supporting more than 9,000 regulated advice professionals who manage about $500bn in assets.

We have proved distribution, trust and demand. The most important infrastructure is still ahead of us.

**Your role**

As a Partner, you will build your own book of clients the way the best advisers build a practice: firms you found, won, and advised for years, with Michelin-grade care from the first conversation to long after the signature. You are the single trusted owner of the relationship, and the all-rounder transformation partner your firms plan their future with.

Saturn is a Series A, Y Combinator-backed company building the AI-native operating system for financial advice. Our platform combines a living data model of the client, AI agents that complete complex advice and operational workflows, and compliance logic embedded directly into how work is produced. The initial wedge is adviser productivity. The larger opportunity is rebuilding the operating model of the advice firm around connected data, intelligent workflows and continuous regulatory control.

This is a full-cycle role with end-to-end ownership. And you’re never carrying it alone: you conduct the whole of Saturn behind your book, with teams of experts supporting your firms’ day-to-day queries and running implementation as each firm needs, while you own the relationship, the strategy and the growth. The timing is the opportunity: Saturn is already the market leader, the UK has thousands of firms ready to move, and the playbook is still being written, by the Partners who join now. Your work will determine whether Saturn becomes the foundational platform through which an entire industry operates.

**The Team**

Our Partnerships team is small and high-calibre by design and works the way we expect advisers to serve their clients: with unreasonable care and long-term commitment. Every Partner carries real revenue responsibility and shapes the go-to-market motion rather than executing someone else’s playbook. What they learn in the market becomes how Saturn sells.

* **The full cycle for new logo IFAs.** Outbound prospecting, inbound qualification, discovery, demos, POCs, business cases, negotiation and close. Consultative selling, not transactional product pitching.
* **Help transform your clients.** Understand where each firm is trying to go, build a clear view of the journey from today to a modern advice business, and challenge constructively where existing ways of working are holding them back.
* **Lead the client relationship.** Own it end to end. Deep trust with senior stakeholders, clear goals and priorities for every firm, risks surfaced early, difficult moments handled with judgement.

### **About Authologic**

You don't need a decade of Fintech experience, but you do bring a strong analytical foundation, technical fluency, and a sharp eye for product quality. * **API Familiarity:** You understand what an API is, have a basic grasp of REST/JSON concepts, and aren't afraid to look at technical integration docs.
* **Strong Business Communication:** You communicate clearly, articulate ideas logically, and feel comfortable talking to both developers and business stakeholders.
* **Fast Learner & Curious Mind:** You absorb new concepts quickly, ask thoughtful questions, and love figuring out _"how things work under the hood."_
* **Languages:** Professional fluency in **both English and Polish** is strictly required (min. C1 level for English to work with global provider docs).
